subject: Proactive security notification + SOC 2 / CAIQ evidence handoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finvera.com>, security@finvera.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proactive security notification + SOC 2 / CAIQ evidence handoff

Hi Alice / FinVera security team —

Quick note from Redwood's security ops: during a routine telemetry audit yesterday evening (2028-05-16 22:43 UTC) our anomaly detectors flagged an elevated number of 403 responses against a small set of API keys tied to a sandbox tenant belonging to FinVera. We ran containment steps immediately and there is no evidence of sensitive data exfiltration. Out of caution we wanted to: 1) notify you, 2) share our IRP artifacts you requested for SOC 2/CAIQ mapping, and 3) propose a short joint timeline for any additional evidence you need.

What we did so far:
- Rotated the three affected API keys and revoked long-lived tokens (completed 2028-05-17 03:05 UTC).
- Captured server-side request logs and exported sanitized redteam traces (see attachment redteam_log_export_20280516.ndjson).
- Triggered a targeted audit run on the sub-account and escalated to incident response engineer (Marissa).

What we are sending now (attached):
- IRP_v2.1.pdf — our incident response playbook excerpt (redacted for internal developer notes).
- CAIQ_mapping_2028-05.xlsx — mapping of CAIQ questions to evidence artifacts + control owners.
- redteam_log_export_20280516.ndjson — sanitized request traces (timestamps, truncated IPs, request IDs).

Can you confirm the preferred evidence ingestion channel (secure SFTP OR your Drive share)? If you want us to push files to your DocuSign/HIPAA vault we can coordinate with Kimberly on logistics.

Proposed short timeline (please adjust):
- Today EOD (PST): confirm receipt of attachments and preferred transfer method.
- Tomorrow 10:00am PT: 30-min call to walk through IRP artifacts and CAIQ mapping.
- By 2028-05-19: provide any additional log slices or redactions you need.

If you need an immediate point of contact, Marissa will handle the forensic exports and I will coordinate the SOC 2 control mappings.

Thanks — wanted to be proactive and avoid surprises during your audit window.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0173

Attachment stubs: IRP_v2.1.pdf (application/pdf), CAIQ_mapping_2028-05.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet), redteam_log_export_20280516.ndjson (application/ndjson)

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finvera.com>

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up and for the swift containment. Appreciate the proactive approach. I confirm receipt of the three attachments. Quick clarifications:

1) Is the ndjson export fully redacted for customer identifiers? We need assurance for our compliance team that PII has been removed.
2) For CAIQ mapping, can you call out which artifacts satisfy: CC-6 (logging) and CM-7 (configuration monitoring)?

Preferred transfer channel: secure SFTP (we will provide creds via our vendor onboarding portal). Please do not upload to any public Drive links.

I can join a walk-through at 10:00am PT tomorrow; I also want our internal incident lead (security@finvera.com) on the call.

— Alice
Alice Chen
Director, Security & Compliance, FinVera
alice.chen@finvera.com

Hi Alice / team —

Thanks for confirming, Alice. Short answers below and a couple of attachments we prepared for the call:

1) Redaction scope: the attached ndjson file has customer_id and user_id fields hashed and the last octet of IP addresses truncated — internal ticket RED-398 documents the redaction script. If you want, we can generate an additional export with only request IDs + timestamps.

2) CAIQ control mapping: the CAIQ_mapping_2028-05.xlsx includes a dedicated tab for CC-6 and CM-7 with artifact pointers:
   - CC-6 (Logging): control satisfied by 'ingest-audit-log' S3 buckets (s3://redwood-ingest/audit/YYYY/MM) plus our internal Splunk retention snapshots (index: infra_audit, retention 365d). Evidence files: logs_splunk_snapshot_20280516.tgz (we will stage to SFTP).
   - CM-7 (Config monitoring): control satisfied by our config-tracker DB (config_changes table) and automated drift alerts (alert id prefix CFG-). Evidence: config_drift_report_20280516.csv.

I will stage additional artifacts to an SFTP drop today. Kimberly — can you confirm SFTP account creation and the hostname?

Action items for the call tomorrow (10:00am PT):
- Quick walkthrough of IRP_v2.1 playbook sections 2.1–2.4.
- Validate CAIQ CA-1/CC-6/CM-7 evidence mappings.
- Confirm any further log slices and agree retention / redaction before transfer to FinVera vault.

Marissa Cole
Incident Response Lead, Redwood Inference
